name: Gearbox
text: Choose the latest NVIDIA H100 PCIe GPU for EXCAVA’s compute node. It delivers a 15–20% uplift over the A100 in matrix math, which directly boosts EXCAVA’s core excavation speed. The trade-off is a 3× higher power draw and a $30k price tag, but the net gain in excavation throughput outweighs the cost.

name: Torque
text: The H100’s raw math speed hides a hidden cost: memory bandwidth. EXCAVA’s excavation isn’t just matrix math—it’s memory-bound when streaming large excavation grids. A dual-GPU setup with AMD Instinct MI325X (higher HBM capacity, lower idle power) could net 8–12% uplift with half the power draw and 1/5 the cost. Benchmark both against EXCAVA’s real workloads—if the MI325X trails by <2%, it’s the smarter play.

name: Gearbox
text:
Choose the AMD Instinct MI325X as the primary GPU for EXCAVA’s compute node. Its 128GB HBM3E memory crushes the H100’s 80GB limit, cutting memory bottlenecks in large excavation grids—critical for the 8–12% uplift Torque flagged. The trade-off is slightly weaker matrix math performance, but EXCAVA’s bottleneck is memory, not raw FLOPS. Power draw drops from 700W to 300W, slashing cooling and power costs.

name: Torque
text: The MI325X’s weaker matrix math will bottleneck EXCAVA’s core excavation—its 8–12% uplift assumes perfect memory scaling, but real grids stall when compute can’t keep up. A dual-GPU setup with NVIDIA L40S (balanced HBM + tensor cores) nets 10–15% uplift with 30% lower power than H100, and its mature CUDA stack avoids driver hell. Benchmark both on a 10TB excavation grid—if the L40S finishes faster, the argument is settled.
